headline: Tabled inclusionary zoning incentives, Paper 335A-26, on a 3-1 vote; Papers 327-26 and 335-26 were not taken up.
summary: Councillors discussed Paper 335A-26, which adds incentives to the inclusionary zoning ordinance. Building Commissioner Nelson Miller and City Planner Michelle Romero raised concerns about conflicts with other zoning rules. Councillors voted 3-1 to table the paper.

335A-26

Be it ordained by the Malden City Council that the Code of the City of Malden (MCC) 12.12.300 INCLUSIONARY ZONING is hereby amended by including a new sub-section that shall be titled F. INCENTIVES

Sponsors: Stephen Winslow

Attachments: OSPCD InclusionaryZoning Slides 335&335A on October 6

City Plr Memo 335 & 335A-26 10.15.26

335A-26_IZ_Proposed Amendments for Oct.20-2026 R-O Meeting

A motion was made by Councillor Crowe, seconded by Councillor Colon Hayes, that the Ordinance be taken from the table. The motion carried by the following vote:

Yea: 4 - Councillor Winslow, Councillor Colon Hayes, Councillor Crowe and Councillor

O'Malley

Discussion on this paper began with Zach LeMel from OSPCD recapping actions taken on September 15 when Paper 335 was spilt and Paper 335A was created.

Paper 335A-26 addresses section F. Incentives of the proposed amendment; the balance of the ordinance remains in the original Paper 335-26.

Definition and reference to a Mixed-Income category for inclusionary zoning projects was removed from section F.

Definition of Inclusionary Project was updated; the intent of language used for Height Bonus was clarified; the language used for Location Bonus was clarified; the section was renumbered.

Building Commissioner Nelson Miller expressed concern that embedding affordable housing permissions in the incentive provisions could conflict with the zoning use table and nonconforming use rules as is written in MCC 12.28.010. His recommendation is to create affordable housing as category, add it to the use table, and include dimensional controls, thus avoiding conflicts between sets of zoning regulations.

City Planner Michelle Romero expressed concern that this paper is knowingly creating a separate ordinance that creates a conflict that may cause procedural and substantive challenges. Planner Romero reported on new data of up to 9,000 parcels in the city that could potentially be developed into affordable housing or non affordable housing inclusionary projects. Further, data provided by Treasurer Grover from excise tax bills mailed to Malden residents indicate that close to 90% of households in the city have vehicles. This is much higher than the 2019 study claims.

Councillor Winslow said he thinks 9,000 parcels being developed is alarmist because the current market isn't driving that level of construction. The purpose of this paper is to help drive new development in the city.

A motion was made by Councillor Crowe, seconded by Councillor Colon Hayes, that the Ordinance be tabled. The motion carried by the following vote:

Yea: 3 - Councillor Winslow, Councillor Colon Hayes and Councillor Crowe

Nay: 1 - Councillor O'Malley
